Convert photon-count spectral irradiance to Watts/m^2/nm.

Source: R/n2W_spec_irradiance.R
n2W_spec_irradiance.Rd

Converts per-bin photon flux (photons m\(^{-2}\) s\(^{-1}\) nm\(^{-1}\), or molar equivalents) to energy-based spectral irradiance in W m\(^{-2}\) nm\(^{-1}\). The inverse operation is W2mol_spec_irradiance.

Usage

n2W_spec_irradiance(value, ...)

# S3 method for class 'numeric'
n2W_spec_irradiance(
  value,
  lambda,
  photonic = FALSE,
  molar_unit = "photons",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lux_spectrum'
n2W_spec_irradiance(value, ...)

Arguments

value

Spectral irradiance in photons/m^2/s/nm (or molar units), or a lux_spectrum with a photonic irradiance or radiance unit.

...

Ignored.

lambda

Wavelength in nm for each bin.

photonic

Logical; if TRUE, value is in molar units (µmol, mmol, or mol/m²/s/nm) — specify which via molar_unit. Defaults to FALSE. Note: photonic = TRUE means raw photon counts in par_irradiance, and photon-or-molar units in irradiance2lux.

molar_unit

Molar unit string (e.g. "umol"). Defaults to "photons".

Value

Numeric vector of spectral irradiance in W/m^2/nm, or a lux_spectrum with unit = "W/m2/nm" or "W/m2/sr/nm" according to the input dimensionality.

Details

Each photon at wavelength \(\lambda\) carries energy \(E = hc/\lambda\). Spectral irradiance in W m\(^{-2}\) nm\(^{-1}\) is therefore the photon flux \(N\) (photons m\(^{-2}\) s\(^{-1}\) nm\(^{-1}\)) multiplied by the per-photon energy: $$E(\lambda) = N(\lambda) \cdot \frac{hc}{\lambda}$$ where \(h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\) J s (Planck constant) and \(c = 2.998 \times 10^8\) m s\(^{-1}\) (speed of light). The constant \(hc\) in nm-compatible units is \(1.98645 \times 10^{-16}\) J nm, the value used internally.

Examples

utils::data(Naples)
n2W_spec_irradiance(Naples$depth_0m, Naples$wv, photonic = TRUE, molar_unit = "umol")
